The story, tap by tap

The 14-step pitch journey

Thandi, a final-year student, from signing in to giving back as an alumna. These are real screenshots, taken by the automated test that runs the journey on every change. Swipe sideways; tap a screen to enlarge it.

Fixed, and measured

A sign-in screen you can read

The first screen set its words over a busy photograph, and they were hard to read. Every line is now set on solid navy, and the photograph fades in above it. An automated audit measures each line of text on a photo screen against the pixels behind it, at three phone widths, on every change.

WCAG AA asks for 4.5 : 1 for body text. All 844 lines of text on photo screens now pass at 320, 360 and 390 points wide.

Beyond the demo

Live mode, through a real backend

The same app, built in live mode, talks to the reference BFF over HTTPS. Sign-in, payments and every screen go through the server, which checks each request against the permission policy and writes sensitive actions to an audit log. An automated test runs all 14 journey steps this way on every change, and another runs the console’s create → approve workflow with staff signed in through the same SSO.

For the teams who run it

The operator console

Communications, faculties, approvers and commerce staff publish into their own areas, and nobody approves their own notice. Every action is permission-checked and written to an audit log; in live mode the server does the checking.

0NMU endpoints invented
  • Product discovery & UX/UI design. Design system on the C.I. palette and Nunito Sans; every flow for four roles, with loading, empty, error, offline and denied states. Text on photographs redesigned so every line passes WCAG AA, measured.
  • Mobile app (iOS, Android, web). 51 screens, four roles, the 14-step pitch journey, offline rules, accessibility patterns, assistant, payments and tickets. Live builds sign in with NMU SSO (code + PKCE), hand payments to the provider and register for push.
  • Operator console. 15 pages: notifications workflow, approvals, audiences, events, commerce, content, moderation, roles, analytics, audit log. In live mode staff sign in with NMU SSO and every action runs on the BFF, as them.
  • Backend (BFF) & system integrations. A reference BFF serving all 65 app routes over mock connectors, and the console’s backend: sessions, the sign-in code exchange, the permission policy and parent consent on every route, ownership checks and an audit log. The live app and the live console both run through it.
  • Security, privacy & compliance. One permission policy, enforced on the server as well as in the app; separation of duties enforced on the server; student-controlled parent consent; PKCE sign-in with single-use codes bound to their client; console and app sessions kept apart; payments only the payer can confirm; no caching of money, results or wellbeing.
  • Testing & accessibility. 154 unit tests, including the BFF’s security boundary; the pitch journey in demo, single-file and live mode; the console workflow in demo and live mode; a 184-screen sweep; 844 lines of text on photographs measured for contrast; WCAG 2.2 AA checks on the console.
  • Hosting, DevOps & release. Continuous integration for the app, the console, and both in live mode against the BFF, plus iOS and Android bundle builds.
  • Project management, content & launch. Brief analysis, documentation, the integration contract with its sign-in, payment and push flows, a go-live checklist and handover.

Checks passing: typecheck, lint and 154 unit tests; the 14-step journey in the demo build, the single-file app and live mode through the BFF; the console workflow in demo and live mode; every screen for four roles at two phone widths; 844 lines of text on photographs at WCAG AA; iOS and Android bundle builds; WCAG 2.2 AA automated checks on all 15 console pages. GitHub Actions runs them on every change.

Audit

How much is left

“Complete” means two different things, so there are two answers.

The prototype: 92% complete

Measured against the brief’s definition of done (§30). What’s left is mostly inputs from NMU, plus device testing:

  • Run the native iOS and Android builds on real phones and fix what turns up. Their bundles build in CI, but everything so far has been run in the web build.
  • NMU confirms the university’s name in the app and supplies the approved logo.
  • The Alumni Mentorship photograph (a stand-in is used today).
  • Protection Services confirms the Campus Protection numbers.
  • Each owner approves or rewrites their help article for the assistant.
  • A manual VoiceOver and TalkBack pass.

A production launch: 43% complete

Real students on real data, in the app stores. About 121 of 214 person-weeks remain. Most of it is connecting NMU’s systems: the BFF they plug into now exists and the live app runs through it, but on stand-in connectors, because the prototype uses demo data by design.

Estimate

What it costs

Priced at South African agency rates for a team covering product, design, mobile, web, backend, QA, security and delivery. A budget estimate for planning, not a quote.

To finish from todayR4.1mRange R2.9m – R6.4m · ≈ US$250kWith 15% contingency: R4.7m
Full build from scratchR7.3mRange R5.1m – R11.3m · ≈ US$441kWith 15% contingency: R8.4m
Work already in placeR3.1m≈ 93 person-weeks at the likely rateWhat the prototype would cost to commission

Timeline and team

  • To launch from today: about 17 weeks of work for a team of 7; plan for 6–8 months, because access to NMU’s systems and approvals set the pace.
  • From scratch: about 31 weeks of work; plan for 9–12 months.
  • Team: a delivery lead or business analyst, a product designer, two app and web developers, two backend and integration developers and a QA and accessibility tester. Part-time: security and DevOps.

Assumptions

  • Blended agency rate R850/hour (range R700–R1,100), 40-hour weeks. Senior developers earn roughly R420–R630/hour employed and bill about US$40–55/hour through outsourcing firms.
  • Effort could run 15% under or 20% over the model, mostly depending on how easily NMU’s systems can be reached.
  • US$1 ≈ R16.50. Excludes VAT, third-party licences and NMU’s own staff time.
  • Scope: everything in the brief, built as one phase. Launching the pitch-journey services first and adding the rest later spreads the cost.

Next steps

What NMU needs to provide

  • Access to systems. API or data access to SSO, the student system, finance, LMS, library, transport, residence and the alumni CRM. The biggest single unknown in the estimate.
  • Identity. An OIDC client registered for NMU ONE with NMU SSO, for the redirects nmuone://auth/callback and the web build’s /auth/callback. The app side is built.
  • Providers. Payment, donations, push notifications and campus mapping. The app already hands payments to a provider’s page and registers devices for push.
  • Policy. Parent access rules, POPIA advice, digital ID approval.
  • Content owners. Named owners for help articles, safety information and notices.

Biggest risk: how NMU’s systems can be reached. Systems with modern APIs keep the integration estimate; systems that need exports, middleware or vendor work push it towards the high end.
